Subject: Can't accept Coupa invite — browser/device fingerprint denied

We received the Coupa invitation this morning but when I click the claim link I get a "403 — access denied" page that mentions a device/browser fingerprint mismatch. We tried Chrome on our Mac and Safari on an iPad. Same result. I attached a screenshot (screenshot-403.png).

This is blocking us from accepting the vendor profile and submitting the W-9 — we have a PO pending and the buyer (Procurement@greenthread.com) is asking for the vendor record to be claimed. Can you help?

Hi Elaine — thanks for the screenshot, sorry for the friction. Looping in Ben (onboarding ops) and Rishi (security) and Laura in AP so we can get you through this today.

Ben/Team — vendor reports a 403 device/browser fingerprint block when trying to claim the Coupa invite. They tried multiple browsers and devices. Attached screenshot shows the Coupa page hinting at an attestation denial. Can we either: (1) reissue a claim link that avoids the attestation check, or (2) provide a one-time magic claim link that skips device fingerprinting?

Laura — buyer has a PO pending; if we need a manual stop-gap (accept vendor on our side and attach W-9 later) please advise on risk and backlog.

Elaine — while we dig in, could you tell us: which browser + exact version, and whether you're behind a corporate VPN or a gateway appliance? That will help Ben reproduce.

Thanks —
Irene Choi

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Can't accept Coupa invite — browser/device fingerprint denied

Hi all — quick troubleshooting steps from our side:

- Elaine: can you paste the browser user agent string (Chrome: chrome://version or Safari: Settings) and confirm if you see any privacy extensions that might block client hints?
- Try an incognito/private window to rule out extension cookie interference.
- If you're on an MDM-managed device (company laptop), some attestation flags can fail. If possible, try a personal phone hotspot (cellular) to rule out gateway-level rewriting.

Temporary workaround options we can do now:
1) Issue a one-time claim link that disables the device attestation check for 30 minutes.
2) Create the vendor record manually in our Coupa admin and link the PO to the manually created vendor — then the vendor can upload W-9 directly to the PO. This requires AP sign-off.

I'll stand up a one-time claim link if you confirm the browser info and give OK for the temporary bypass.

Attachment: greenthread-claim.pdf (we don't need content but noting their internal W-9 claim flow)

—Ben

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 11 Jun 2028 10:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Can't accept Coupa invite — browser/device fingerprint denied

Quick note on security/ops:

- The "device fingerprint" block likely comes from our WAF module that enforces attestation for third-party invites when we see high entropy in client hints or when headers are stripped by a gateway. I don't want to broadly turn that off, but a scoped bypass for this claim link is safe if we: (a) restrict by the vendor email domain (greenthread.com), (b) set a 20-minute TTL, and (c) log the claim IP and user agent for audit.
- Ben — please capture the request ID from our Coupa proxy logs when this next attempt happens; I'll pull audit logs and confirm there was no suspicious activity.

Laura — AP: if we need to accept vendor record manually, note that the manual creation flow requires a compliance checklist sign-off. If you want me to expedite the audit review for this one vendor, I can clear it by EOD if Ben provides the logs.

Rishi
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

From: Elaine Soto <elaine@greenthread.com>

Subject: Re: Can't accept Coupa invite — browser/device fingerprint denied

Thanks everyone — we tried the incognito window and that worked. Ben created a temporary one-time claim link that let us finish claiming the vendor profile; we uploaded the W-9 and confirmed the vendor contact. I've attached the confirmation PDF from our side (greenthread-claim.pdf).

Procurement will proceed with PO acceptance; please let me know if you need any additional audit info — happy to provide the user agent and IP if needed. Appreciate the fast help.

Elaine
